task.description: WF-02, step 3 — SECURITY-REVIEWER, gate, on the change of step 2 (handoffs/E2E106-20261115-01/step-02-backend-dev.json): tools/test/e2e/kit/stand.js, tools/test/fixtures/e2e-stand/fake-stand.js, tools/README.md (diff against the tag base/E2E106-20261115-01), by the design docs/design/REQ-106-e2e-pixel-office.md (sections 4.1, 4.2, 5, 6) and decisions/0112 (О1, О13, О14, О16) and decisions/0109 О15. Your area here is R2 and the safety of the owner's computer: the starter must never let a stand reach the person's real home folder or the real Pixel Office state folder, through HOME or USERPROFILE, through stateEnv, through a value of env (also after '='), through an argument (also after '=', and the first-argument exemption), through links, '..', a relative path, a path equal to the temporary root in any spelling, a path inside the repository; and the refusal must come before the marker and before any spawn (protection in the same operation as the action). Try to break it yourself: write attack cases on copies outside the project (a clone of the tag with the work files copied in), each with the spawn that records and throws for any call that names a real folder (rule R2-S of the design, section 6), and report each case with the result. Also check: the private home is created with mode 0700 and removed on every path; STAND_HOME_WRITTEN and its precedence; the stand-in's own guard (it writes only strictly under its real temporary root); what the README says against what the code does; secrets and messages (safeText on new messages, the open defect ISS-0110). Step 4 (REVIEWER) runs at the same time on the same files; do not coordinate, judge alone. The three red starter tests E2S-01, E2S-03, E2S-05 are expected (EXPECTED_RED until step 5). R2, strict: never start Pixel Office, its hook or the stand-in with the real home or the real state folder; record sha256, size and time of all five real files before your first trial and after your last. Change no project file other than this handoff; no commit, push or pull. The handoff holds no absolute machine paths, no temporary paths and no names of other projects of the owner. Verdict PASS or FAIL with findings ranked (Critical, High, Medium block).

MAP OF SURFACES. stand.js: 'comes from outside' (the options a spec passes - args, env, stateEnv - are input, checked by rule P), 'the server goes by itself'/R2 (it spawns a Sai server, the central R2 concern: a stand must never reach the person's real home or the real Pixel Office state folder), 'writes files' (it makes a private home and a marker under the temporary root). fake-stand.js: 'writes files'/R2 (mode write-home writes into its home only under its own real temporary root - its own guard), 'comes from outside' (test-controlled env). No page file changed (no 'goes to the browser' page surface); the starter's error text reaches the console/logs/handoffs and so meets the text-as-text concern through safeText. ITEMS. Q7 secrets: APPLICABLE and MET - no secret in the change or in the files a browser gets (the only grep hit is the word 'token' in a comment naming what the base env list excludes); the child env is built from a named base list only (PATH, TMPDIR, TEMP, TMP, LANG, LC_ALL, TZ, SystemRoot), never the whole shell env; messages hold no env value and no secret. Q8 customer spaces: NOT APPLICABLE - no customer data, no business space (test infrastructure; Pixel Office has one local owner). Q9 SQL: NOT APPLICABLE - no query. Q10 failures: APPLICABLE and MET - every error path is explicit with a code (USAGE, PATH_REFUSED, STAND_START_FAILED, STAND_HOME_WRITTEN, STAND_STOP_TIMEOUT, STAND_EXIT), text goes through safeText, no crash. Q11 external addresses: APPLICABLE and MET in the narrow sense - the server link is checked by assertLoopbackUrl (only http://127.0.0.1:<port>/); no client-supplied address is dialled. R2 Pixel Office / owner's machine: APPLICABLE, CENTRAL, and MET - see the attacks below. R3 photos: NOT APPLICABLE (product dropped, decision 0033; no photo introduced). TWO CHECKS THE MAP REQUIRES. 'writes files' - the path never leaves its own folder: the private home and the marker are made under the temporary root (makeTempDir uses assertOutsideRepo(tempRoot) then mkdtemp), rule P refuses any caller path that is not under the temporary root, is the root itself, or is inside the repository; the stand-in writes only strictly under its own real temporary root. 'goes to the browser' text-as-text - the starter's messages show external text as an escaped string (safeText), not as markup; the one gap is bidi controls, which is the open LOW ISS-0110, not new. SHARED MECHANISM (AP-014): rule P is applied consistently to stateEnv, to env values, and to arguments (checkedPath / checkedValue / checkedScript), with the first-argument exemption applied to arg[0] only (verified arg[1] is not exempt); the 'home strictly under the real temporary root' logic is the same in the starter (private home, STAND_HOME_WRITTEN) and in the stand-in (writeHome guard). findings.item: Q10 text-as-text / R2 message hygiene; open defect ISS-0110
findings.place: tools/test/e2e/kit/stand.js:355-361 (STAND_HOME_WRITTEN uses safeText) via tools/test/e2e/kit/errors.js safeText/isControl
findings.what: STAND_HOME_WRITTEN is a new caller of safeText, which escapes C0/C1/DEL/U+2028/U+2029 but lets the bidirectional controls (U+202A-U+202E, U+2066-U+2069, U+200E, U+200F, U+061C) through - the open LOW defect ISS-0110. Confirmed by calling safeText from the clone: a newline is escaped and a leading '::' neutralised, but U+202E and U+2066 pass unescaped. A home-entry name with such a control could read reordered in the runner's console/log.
findings.fix: None in this run. This is already the open LOW ISS-0110; the design records STAND_HOME_WRITTEN as one more caller (section 20) and DOC-UPDATER adds the caller at step 10. Not a new or blocking finding; raised here only to confirm it is the known defect, not a new leak.

findings.item: Q12 accuracy of a documentation reference (REVIEWER/DOC area, not security)
findings.place: tools/README.md, paragraph 'Servers for the page specs' ('... fails stop() with STAND_HOME_WRITTEN (decisions/0109)')
findings.what: The README cites decisions/0109 for STAND_HOME_WRITTEN, but this convention (private home, stateEnv, rule P, STAND_HOME_WRITTEN) is settled in decisions/0112 O1, which closes the precondition O15 of 0109. The code behaviour is correct; only the citation points at the parent decision rather than the one that defines the rule.
findings.fix: Optional: cite decisions/0112 (or 0112 and 0109). Non-security; for REVIEWER or DOC-UPDATER. Not blocking.

findings.item: R2 known limit of rule P (design-acknowledged, BACKEND-DEV I6)
findings.what: Rule P treats a value as a path only when the absolute path is the whole value or the part after the FIRST '=', and it does not check cwd. Neither reaches the real home or the real state folder: an env value like a=b=<path> cannot redirect Pixel Office (SAI_PIXEL_OFFICE_DIR must itself be an absolute path or Pixel Office refuses it - F12; HOME/USERPROFILE are always the private home, set last and un-overridable by env); cwd does not point the state folder (Pixel Office derives it from SAI_PIXEL_OFFICE_DIR or HOME, never from cwd). Verified: env FOO='--dir=<real state>' is refused (after the first '='); the accepted env-inspection case shows the child HOME is the private home even when the parent HOME is the real home.
findings.fix: None required; recorded as a known, bounded limit (matches BACKEND-DEV issue I6 and design section 4.1). Not blocking.

issues.text: F1 is the open LOW defect ISS-0110, not a new leak: STAND_HOME_WRITTEN is one more caller of safeText, which lets bidirectional controls through. The design already records this (section 20) and DOC-UPDATER adds the caller at step 10. No action for this gate.
F2 (README cites decisions/0109 for STAND_HOME_WRITTEN rather than 0112) is a documentation accuracy point for REVIEWER (step 4) or DOC-UPDATER (step 10), not a security defect. Non-blocking.

F3 records the two known, bounded limits of rule P (only the part after the FIRST '=' is a path; cwd is not checked), matching BACKEND-DEV issue I6 and design section 4.1. Neither reaches the real home or the real state folder. Non-blocking.
